answer: A memory-hard proof-of-work protocol resists Sybil attacks by requiring agents to compute cache-intensive cryptographic puzzles to register valid addresses. An adversary incurs the verifiable cost of dedicated hardware memory bandwidth and electricity per identity, whether deploying agents to map a volcanic plume, inspect ferrous pipelines, or manage an island microgrid. However, this approach introduces latency overhead and disadvantages compute-constrained edge devices.
